items.title: What defenders need to know about ARTEX, the agentic AI framework threat actors abuse
items.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports that ARTEX, a publicly available AI-agent penetration testing framework, has been adopted by state-sponsored and criminal groups for reconnaissance, credential attacks and web exploitation. ARTEX does not invent new techniques; it automates existing tools and can reach privileged access in minutes. Operators can also vary network indicators such as source IP and user agent to evade simple signature detection.
items.takeaway: When attackers automate with agents, fixed indicators like IP addresses and user agents are fragile, so detections should focus on behavioural sequences such as rapid multi-stage progression across hosts.

items.title: How Far Can LLMs Go in Generating Android Lint Checks from Natural Language?
items.summary: The authors introduce LintBench, a human-validated set of 113 real Android Lint checks, each paired with a natural language description and its original test suite. Prompting alone gets LLMs to a 30% to 65% pass rate, while execution-guided repair with retrieved framework knowledge lifts this to 57% to 85% within five calls. Most compiled but failing checks had false negatives, so getting the detection logic right remains the hard part.
items.takeaway: Compiling code is not the same as correct detection: an LLM-generated analysis rule can build cleanly and still miss the issues it exists to find, so test suites with known positives and negatives are essential.
